text:
Maya (PM): heads up — SnowPeak just hit 500s on Redwood Dedicated when they send a custom `X-SP-Auth` header. Sales marked this as customer-impacting and asking for a fast patch.

Priya (AE): SnowPeak says this started after they upgraded their middleware. They can tolerate a short maintenance window; they asked whether we can do a scoped patch vs waiting for the next release.

Oliver (Support): attaching relevant snippet from their logs: `2026-02-18T21:03:12Z ERROR handler.go:142 validation failed: header X-SP-Auth: unexpected token` — appears to be parsing edge case when header contains `|` char. Repro steps in support ticket #SP-1245.

Sam (Eng): thanks — looks like our auth header parser rejects certain non-alnum when `strictHeaders=true`. Quick mitigation: fallback to permissive parser for dedicated customers behind feature flag. I can do a targeted patch (small change) + unit test.

Maya (PM): tradeoffs? hotfix vs next minor? Customers want fast fix, but we need canary and rollback plan. Also need comms to SnowPeak and internal routing for billing if they want expedited SR.

Sam (Eng): hotfix seems low-risk if we scope to Dedicated only and gate by a runtime flag `feature.permissive_sp_auth=true`. Patch delta ~10 LOC, add test + e2e. Time estimate: 3-4 hours dev + 2 hours QA + deployment.

Nia (SRE): canary plan ok: roll to 5% on us-east-2 for 30m, monitor 5xx and latency. If green, promote to 100% over 1 hour. Need a rollback knob and a config to kill the flag. Also want a perf smoke test pre-canary.

Priya (AE): SnowPeak wants a clear ETA and a comm template to send to their ops team. They requested we avoid a full outage. They're fine with a canary and asking for an update in 2 hours.

Maya (PM): decision: do targeted hotfix deployed as canary -> 5% -> promote if metrics OK. Assignments: Sam owner for patch + tests, Nia owner for canary rollout and monitoring, Priya will send customer comms once we have ETA. I will draft customer-facing note.

Sam (Eng): starting branch `hotfix/sp-auth-permissive-snowpeak`. Patch preview:
```
// fallback to permissive parsing for SP header when flag enabled
if cfg.GetBool("feature.permissive_sp_auth") {
  headerVal = permissiveParse(rawHeader)
} else {
  headerVal = strictParse(rawHeader)
}
```
I'll open PR in ~45m.

Oliver (Support): adding ticket link SP-1245 to PR. Also adding a support test case with SnowPeak's header sample.

DeployBot: Canary rollout scheduled by Nia — patch `hotfix/sp-auth-permissive-snowpeak` will be deployed to canary pool `dedicated-canary-5pct` at 2026-02-18T23:00:00Z.

Nia (SRE): pre-canary checklist: 1) smoke tests green, 2) alert dashboard has 5xx and P95 latency, 3) rollback runbook ready. Sam pls ping when PR merged.

Sam (Eng): PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/4721 — includes unit tests and permissive parser. Requesting review from @Nia and @Oliver.

Maya (PM): Priya, please send SnowPeak this short note: "We plan a targeted patch deployed as a 5% canary in ~3 hours; we'll update you after canary validation and before full promotion. No expected user-facing downtime." I'll review before send.

Priya (AE): will send after I get approximate completion time from Sam.

Nia (SRE): canary started. DeployBot shows `dedicated-canary-5pct` active. Monitoring hooks live.

DeployBot: Canary started: 5% traffic -> `hotfix/sp-auth-permissive-snowpeak` (us-east-2).

Nia (SRE): initial 15m metrics: 5xx count -> 0, P95 latency -> +8ms (within threshold). No errors in auth parser.

Maya (PM): great. Sam, after we promote, we need release note blurb and internal incident update so support knows how to reference. Also confirm whether this should be cherry-picked to on-prem/offline bundle.

Sam (Eng): will promote to 100% in 30m if metrics hold. I'll add release note and include cherry-pick for the private deployment packaging.

Priya (AE): emailed SnowPeak with the ETA and will notify after full promotion.

Oliver (Support): closing support ticket loop; leaving note on SP-1245 with PR and canary results.

Maya (PM): final: promote done, patch at 100% across Dedicated, release note drafted, support updated, customer notified. Marking this thread resolved — thanks all :tada:
